note: The first byte of the fuzz input selects the target architecture/mode and controls the disassembly path.
The disassembly routine allocates the instruction cache that later carries decoded instruction state.
Per-instruction detail storage is allocated before decoding and then populated by the backend.
When decoding fails and skipdata is enabled, the code copies attacker-controlled bytes into the instruction cache; the benchmark target is the resulting uninitialized-value path in later consumers.
